blocks.text: The descriptions in verses 1–9 are not meant as literal measurements. This kind of body-description poem uses animals, buildings, cultivated plants, and landscape to trace the lover’s gaze through imaginative comparison. The shifting images make beauty vivid and abundant rather than reducing the woman to a physical inventory.

Across the Song, comparable ancient love poetry helps place its alternating voices, body praise, fragrance, and landscapes within a wider poetic world, without establishing one direct source or a cult ritual behind the book. The Song also gives both lovers speech, initiative, praise, longing, and desire; the woman’s invitation and declaration in this chapter belong to that active pattern.
